text:
maya: Heads-up — saw several customers with apparent double token usage after yesterday's routing canary. Pattern is streaming reconnect + tool-call truncation. Anyone else seeing this?

jonathan: Yikes. Any quick repro or trace IDs?

priya: Got traces. Repro is pretty small: client stream disconnects, reconnects to fallback, runtime replays prefix and issues toolcall at resume. Ledger shows both provisional charge for the replayed prefix/toolcall and then final confirmed charge after completion.

asher: Sounds like provisional vs confirmed lifecycle isn't getting deduped for handoffs. We saw something similar when session affinity changes mid-stream.

li: Logs show the canary path changed session_id on the handoff (sticky routing lost), so the idempotency key differs. Toolcall idempotency relies on `X-Session-ID` which changed.

deploy-bot: Deploy: routing-canary reverted at 03:12 UTC — rollback executed.

maya: Revert stops new incidents but we need a follow-up: telemetry, billing reconcile, and a console UX guard for rollouts that alter session affinity keys. Current dashboards only show aggregate tokens, can't surface provisional vs confirmed split.

priya: Proposal for telemetry: add metrics `redwood.tokens.provisional`, `redwood.tokens.confirmed`, `redwood.reconnect.deduped_count`. Alert if provisional/confirmed ratio > 1.1 for > 5m.

jonathan: Also need a reconciliation job to detect overlapped toolcalls across sessions and credit back provisional spikes into provisional-reconcile queue.

asher: Mitigation idea in runtime: when resuming a stream, if `session_id` != `prev_session_id`, suppress emitting provisional ledger entries for toolcalls until final ack or a short coalescing window (e.g., 2s).

li: Agree. A TTL guard is cheaper than full session state sync across hosts. We should be careful with long pauses though — window must be short.

maya: I'll take the dashboard PR to expose provisional vs confirmed and add the alert. Priya, can you own telemetry schema and the metric tags? Asher, can you prototype the TTL guard in runtime? Jonathan, please own the billing reconcile job.

priya: Will post schema sketch and event examples in #infra after lunch. Example event header we plan to emit:

```
X-Session-ID: {{session_id}}
X-Toolcall-Id: {{toolcall_id}}
ledg_event: {"type":"provisional","tokens":42,"session_id":"..."}
```

jonathan: I'll run a one-off mapreduce to find sessions with overlapping toolcall_id sequences and flag affected customer invoices.

maya: Action items + owners noted. Also, console UX ask: before enabling canaries, surface a warning if the rollout config changes session id derivation or idempotency header. That might prevent this class of regression.

asher: Good point — runtime can expose a `session-affinity-stability` boolean in the rollout API; console can block or warn if false.

li: I'll add a short log-level flag to capture session-id changes during handoff for better forensics.

maya: Thanks everyone. Follow-up: priya will paste schema, jonathan will kick off reconcile, asher and li will prototype runtime guard/logging, maya will open dashboard PR.

priya: I'll also add unit+integration tests for reconnect+truncation paths.

jonathan: :thumbsup:

maya: Closing thread for now — will link the postmortem doc once owners create it.
_notes: This thread records an eng-platform discussion about reconnect-related double-billing for streaming + toolcalls, mitigation and telemetry/console followups. Messages are short to match Slack style.
